next_step: Execute scale POC (ingest 100M vectors) — validate batching and KV-cache gains
notes:
Background: Meridian is an enterprise marketplace (seller catalogs + historical transactions). Target index size: 300M–800M product+session vectors. Primary pain: existing vector store can't scale cost-effectively; high tail latency at 99th pctl during peak campaigns.

POC scope: ingest 100M vectors (mixed dense + metadata), test offline reranker with 2-stage flow (ANN -> rerank with cross-encoder), measure end-to-end p99 and cost/token/query. Also evaluate prefix/KV caching to reduce reranker compute for repeated queries.

Perf targets:
- E2E p95 < 120ms during steady-state queries
- E2E p99 < 450ms at 1k qps sustained
- Cost per query target <$0.002 for ANN+rerank (on average)

Security/compliance: require SSO (SAML), enterprise KMS integration, per-customer audit logs, data residency for EU/NA shards. Legal needs DPA and vendor penetration report.

Recent notes from calls:
- "We need to see 3x reduction in unit cost vs our hosted vector infra to proceed." — Director of Search
- SE call 2026-02-28: reviewed shard/ingest approach; Redwood suggested batching + async ingest pipeline. Action: provide sample ingestion script and S3 presigned batch job.
- Infosec sent initial questionnaire (link in Drive). Next: complete penetration assessment and provide SOC2 Type II evidence.

Technical constraints:
- Data is stored in S3 (multi-region), ~3PB raw, vectors computed offline.
- Need managed rollout for reranker model changes, traffic-splitting for experiments.
- Prefers GPU deduplication and quantized float16/8 support to minimize memory footprint.

Next steps (short):
- Share ingestion checklist and sample manifest (Redwood)
- Schedule infra sizing call for 100M POC (SE + infra)
- Provide cost model comparison (Redwood vs in-house) by 2026-03-10

Opportunity notes: Large expansion potential if POC meets latency/cost targets — could convert to dedicated pools + multi-region private deployment. Upsell: Optimize package (automated batching/caching) likely.
